transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

A 9-year-old Indesit washing machine that fills and drains but doesn't spin is often fixable, but the cost depends on the specific fault. The most common cause for this exact symptom (water moves, drum stays still) is a broken drive belt, which is an inexpensive part to replace. Other possibilities include worn motor carbon brushes or a failed motor. If it's just the belt, it's usually well worth repairing. Could you please check if the drive belt is intact? With the machine unplugged, lay it on its back (or access the rear panel) and look for a black rubber belt around the drum. Is the belt still there and intact, or is it broken/missing?

I've taken the back panel off and the belt is on the pulleys and feels tight, so it doesn't look like the belt. I should mention that I noticed a faint hot electrical smell a few weeks ago, though not since. What should I look at next?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning smell or smoke can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The belt being intact and that past hot electrical smell strongly point to a motor issue. On Indesit machines like yours (which typically use brushed motors), the most common cause for 'fills/drains but no spin' combined with an electrical smell is worn carbon brushes inside the motor. As they wear down, they lose contact with the motor's commutator, stopping it from turning. Please check if you can see the two brush holders on the back of the motor (usually accessible once the belt is off or by looking at the rear caps). Are the brushes still long enough to be pressing firmly against the metal ring inside, or do they look very short/worn? If they are worn down short, replacing them is a cheap and straightforward fix.

I've unplugged it and left it off, as you say. I took the two carbon brushes out of the motor. One is very short and blackened or charred at the tip, and the other is a bit longer. Does that look like the cause to you?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
That confirms it. The motor needs good contact from both brushes to spin; with one worn down like that, it simply cannot turn the drum. You need to replace both carbon brushes as a set (even though only one looks bad) to ensure even wear and reliable operation. This is typically an inexpensive part for Indesit machines. Once you have fitted the new pair, reassemble the motor and back panel, plug the machine back in, and it should spin normally again. If you are comfortable doing this yourself, buy a matching carbon brush kit for your model series. If you would prefer not to do the fitting, take this diagnosis to an engineer—they will likely just replace the brushes.
